Full-Time  Smithfield, NSW 

Keep Things Moving Behind the Scenes

This is a hands-on sales support role suited to someone who enjoys working with systems, processing orders and coordinating information across different teams.
You will play an important role in supporting the sales function, ensuring customer orders are processed accurately, system information is maintained and communication between customers, sales, production, warehouse and logistics runs efficiently.

  • The ability to work collaboratively across multiple teams in a busy environment.

  • Full-time opportunity within an established Australian manufacturing business.
  • Stable working environment with a supportive and collaborative team.
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities.
  • The opportunity to develop your skills across sales operations, systems and administration.

  • $80,000 + Super
  • Permanent full-time opportunity
  • Immediate start available

job.title: Operational Safety Manager
job.description:
Operational Safety Manager   |  Western Sydney  |  $170K to $180K + Super

The Company:

Step into a fast-growing, privately-owned operator in a highly regulated, safety-critical industry, with an evolving and expanding service offering. Safety isn't a compliance box here. It's a genuine leadership priority, backed by real authority and real investment, and our client is looking for someone who wants to help shape what safety looks like, not just maintain what already exists.

This is a newly defined Operational Safety Manager role, created because the business is ready to invest properly in safety leadership, not just fill a gap. It comes with a clear runway to a broader Head of Safety and Compliance position for the right person, giving you a real say in how the function grows from here.

The Position:

Reporting directly to the General Manager, you'll take genuine ownership of operational safety, not oversight from a distance, leading a ground-up review of current procedures with the mandate to reshape how safety works from day one.

What you'll be doing:
  • Leading a full, ground-up review of current safety procedures and driving practical improvements
  • Rebuilding and maintaining SWMS, risk assessments and safe operating procedures
  • Owning incident and near-miss investigations end to end, from first response and root cause analysis through to corrective actions and close-out
  • Building operational readiness for dangerous goods handling and storage, including training, risk assessments and emergency response procedures
  • Leading safety training, coaching and toolbox talks across drivers, plant operators and site teams
  • Driving a genuine, measurable shift in safety culture, particularly building trust and buy-in within driver and operational teams
  • Overseeing Chain of Responsibility and heavy vehicle safety at the operational level, including fatigue, loading and scheduling risk
  • Managing Return to Work and Workers Compensation cases from notification through to resolution
  • Coordinating emergency preparedness, including planning, drills, and post-incident review
  • Exercising full stop-work authority where you identify unsafe activity, backed by senior leadership
  • Partnering closely with senior operational leaders across the business to embed safety into day-to-day decision-making
  • Reporting on safety performance and trends to the General Manager, with a clear line of sight to broader compliance and business risk
The Candidate:

We're looking for someone genuinely progressive in how they think about safety, someone who sees it as a driver of performance and culture, not just a regulatory requirement. This role suits an experienced, dynamic safety leader who wants to build and shape something, not simply administer an existing system.

You'll bring:
  • Significant experience in a senior operational safety or WHS leadership role within transport, waste, logistics, industrial or another high-risk, regulated environment
  • Solid working knowledge of Chain of Responsibility, NHVR requirements, and heavy vehicle or bulk transport safety
  • A strong track record of leading incident investigations and translating findings into real, followed procedures
  • Genuine comfort operating in yards, depots and vehicles, not a desk-bound safety professional
  • The confidence to challenge unsafe practices and influence change at every level of a business, regardless of commercial pressure
  • Experience with, or strong exposure to, dangerous goods, chemical handling or petrochemical environments (highly regarded, not essential)
  • Background with a larger, structured logistics or industrial organisation is a plus, but we're just as open to a hands-on operator from a smaller business who's ready to step up
The Benefits:
  • $170,000 to $180,000 + super
  • A newly created role with genuine scope to shape safety strategy and execution from day one
  • A clear, realistic progression pathway to a Head of Safety and Compliance role
  • Full authority and senior leadership backing to make safety decisions that matter
  • Involvement in a major growth initiative: the safe expansion into dangerous goods
  • A hands-on, high-impact culture where your work is visible and valued, not lost in bureaucracy
  • The chance to build modern, practical safety systems in a business that's genuinely investing in getting it right

job.description:

Step into a fast-paced Senior HR Business Partner contract where you can quickly build relationships, support leaders and make an immediate impact.

You’ll join the Australian operation of a well-established global organisation, working as part of an experienced HR team within a professional services environment.

  • Coach and support managers across people and performance matters

job.title: Perishable Cargo Logistics & Documentation Officer
job.description:
Export Logistics & Documentation Specialist
$90,000 - $95,000 + Super
Central Parramatta | Walking Distance to Train & Bus Interchange

Are you currently working in meat, protein, chilled, frozen or perishable exports and ready to take ownership of the entire export process?
We're partnering with a growing Australian-owned international trading and export business that supplies food and grocery products across global markets. As the business continues to expand, they are looking to add two experienced Export Logistics & Documentation Specialists to their high-performing team.
This is an opportunity to join a business where your role extends well beyond documentation. You'll play a key part in coordinating international shipments, managing supplier relationships, solving logistics challenges, and ensuring products move seamlessly from origin through to delivery.

Why This Opportunity Stands Out
  • Growing international business with genuine career progression opportunities
  • End-to-end ownership of export operations
  • Exposure to global food and protein supply chains
  • Fast-paced, varied environment where no two days are the same
  • Central Parramatta location with easy access to train, bus and light rail
  • Supportive team that values initiative and accountability
  • $90,000 - $95,000 + Super
The Role
Working closely with suppliers, customers, freight providers and internal stakeholders, you'll manage international shipments from order creation through to final delivery.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Coordinating end-to-end export shipments across air freight, sea freight, LCL and consolidation movements
  • Preparing and managing export documentation including:
    • Commercial Invoices
    • Packing Lists
    • Health Certificates
    • Certificates of Origin
    • Bills of Lading
  • Managing purchase orders and sales orders
  • Liaising with suppliers, freight forwarders, shipping lines and 3PL providers
  • Monitoring shipment schedules, inventory availability and customer commitments
  • Resolving operational issues, delays and supply chain challenges
  • Reviewing supplier and freight invoices
  • Maintaining reporting and shipment visibility across the supply chain
About You
We're particularly interested in candidates who have worked within:
  • Meat and protein exports
  • Frozen food exports
  • Chilled and perishable products
  • Seafood exports
  • Food manufacturing or food trading businesses
  • Temperature-controlled supply chains
You'll also bring:
  • Experience managing international export shipments end-to-end
  • Strong export documentation knowledge
  • Excellent stakeholder management and customer service skills
  • Strong attention to detail and problem-solving ability
  • A proactive, hands-on approach in a fast-moving environment
Meat industry experience is highly prized and will be viewed very favourably.
Candidates from frozen, chilled, seafood and broader perishable export environments are also strongly encouraged to apply.
Please Note : This is not a pure freight forwarding role.
Whilst freight forwarding experience is certainly welcomed as part of your career background, we're looking for professionals who have worked across the broader export and supply chain function, including documentation, customer service, supplier coordination, inventory management and operational logistics.
 
If you've built your career in meat, protein, frozen or perishable exports and want to join a growing business where you can genuinely own the export process, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: WHS Advisor
job.description:
$130,000 + super | Parramatta | Hybrid

Step into a broad WHS Advisor role where your advice, judgement and stakeholder influence will make a real impact across safety, workers compensation, injury management and return to work.

Joining a well-established, purpose-led organisation with 500 + employees across multiple locations, you’ll work closely with the senior People & Culture leader, broader HR team and operational leaders to provide practical advice, strengthen safety awareness and support positive injury management outcomes.

This is an established role with strong foundations in place, allowing you to focus on partnering with leaders, managing BAU matters and continuing to improve safety practices across the organisation.

The Role
Reporting to the senior People & Culture leader, you’ll act as a trusted WHS Advisor to operational and senior leaders across corporate and frontline environments.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Advising leaders on WHS risks, incidents, injury management and appropriate actions
  • Managing workers compensation, return-to-work and personal injury matters
  • Developing and managing individual return-to-work plans
  • Working closely with employees, managers, insurers and external providers to achieve timely outcomes
  • Reviewing incidents and supporting or coordinating workplace investigations
  • Maintaining and improving WHS policies, procedures, risk registers and reporting
  • Supporting WHS inductions, training and safety awareness initiatives
  • Monitoring hazards, incidents and injury trends and identifying areas for improvement
  • Working with the insurer on claims and workers compensation premium management
  • Preparing WHS data and insights for monthly Board reporting
  • Conducting site visits and risk assessments as required
About You
You’ll be a confident, pragmatic WHS professional who can work autonomously, build credibility quickly and provide clear, practical advice to managers.
You will ideally bring:
  • Experience in a broad WHS, injury management and workers compensation role
  • SIRA Return to Work Coordinator accreditation and experience managing NSW workers compensation claims
  • Experience managing workplace and non-work-related injuries
  • Exposure to psychosocial claims or psychosocial risk management
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and confidence advising operational and senior leaders
  • Experience within a larger, multi-site employer; frontline, operational, environments would be highly regarded
  • A practical, empathetic and solutions-focused communication style
  • Strong reporting skills and intermediate Excel capability
  • The ability to work independently while collaborating closely with HR and operational teams
  • Current driver’s licence
  • A relevant WHS or related qualification is preferred.
Why This Role?
This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to be a true advisor.

You’ll have genuine ownership, regular interaction with senior and operational leaders, and the support of the senior People & Culture leader and HR team. The focus is on helping managers make sound decisions, improving safety awareness and supporting employees back to work effectively.

If you’re an experienced WHS professional who enjoys stakeholder engagement, injury management and practical safety advice, we’d love to hear from you.
